title: Early Los Angeles bandleaders: Irving Brothers, Rebb Spikes, Earl Dancer, Edith Turnham
summary: Lee responds to Chilton's names of early thirties Los Angeles bands and adds Edith Turnham, whose son Floyd played lead alto.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Okay. And there was a reference to Earl Dancer under Buck Clayton and Chilton said that Buck Clayton, during the early 30's worked in the L.A. bands led by the Irving Brothers. Is that a name you recognize?
Yeah, but I can't remember them. But it seems like there was some brothers -- yeah. You read
that someplace, huh?
Yeah, in the Chilton book.

Yeah, there were some Irving Brothers, but ... yeah, they were early, though. Yeah, they were. It seems like one played guitar and another one played bad piano. I think ... I don't know. But yeah, I remember the names -- but I think this was a little bit before I got out there.
And then the next name it lists is Ellighew. Duke Ellighue. Was there such a band in Los Angeles?

Duke Ellighue? No. It could have been, but see, to me, it would have made more sense now that you said that, I just thought of ... see, when like before I got here, you know, we got here in 1929 and I don't remember any of those bands. It could have been during that time that I was in school, like from '29 to '33 that I may have lost contact with those people.

But I remember when I first came here, in '29, the guy that they were talking about most, his name was Rebb Spikes. That's the guy that seemed to have had -- and Jack McVea's dad was getting all the gigs, the banjo player. But that Ellighew, I don't remember hearing that.
Lavern Floyd?
Uh huh, yeah. Uh huh. Yeah, I heard that one.
And then it says Charlie Echols and
Earl Dancer. In 1934, when Clayton became the leader of Dancer's 14 piece band.

That was right. I'm sure that was Earl Dancer's band at first. But there's a lady -- they make no reference to Edith Turnham? Floyd Turnham's mother -- there's an Edith Turnham, she played piano and she had a band, and her son played with the band.
We did not find any Turnham in that book.
You didn't? Well, no, she had a band in Los Angeles at one time, and she used to have some good jobs.
What did she play?
She played piano, and her son was a very good lead alto player. His name was Floyd Turnham. Now he ended up playing with Les Hyte in later years.
Is that T-u-r-n-h-a-m?
Uh huh. Yes.
How big a band?
She used to have like 10 or 11 I think.
And that was what? Early 30's?
Uh huh.
